findings.title: Server constructor installs the shared header interceptor before its https check, leaving it active after a rejected construction
Federation lookup follows HTTP redirects past the https-only check, allowing plaintext hops or internal hosts
verifyChallengeTxSigners does not bind the verified signers to the challenge's client account
verifyChallengeTxSigners does not bind the verified signers to the challenge's client account
Unvalidated domain in stellar.toml fetch allows requests to arbitrary or internal hosts
Config.setTimeout is documented as global but only federation and TOML requests honour it
HTTP error branch in federation request handler is unreachable, so callers get raw axios errors instead of BadResponseError
Horizon rejections never reach the BadResponseError branch, so callers lose the result codes
transaction(hash) silently drops filters already set on the builder
forAssetPair native branch leaves stale base/counter code and issuer query parameters on reuse
forLedger accepts unvalidated string sequence and passes it into the URL path
Native branch of buying()/selling() leaves stale asset code and issuer query parameters on a reused OfferCallBuilder
ledger(sequence) pushes an unvalidated value into the Horizon ledger path filter
Native branch of selling() leaves stale selling asset code and issuer query parameters on a reused OfferCallBuilder
Config.setTimeout is documented as global but only federation and TOML requests honour it
AccountResponse copies raw Horizon keys onto the instance, so a "__proto__" key replaces the object's prototype
submitTransaction rejects with a generic error after a possibly successful send and gives no hash for reconciliation
Process-wide allowHttp flag lets one Config call enable plaintext transport for every later Server, FederationServer and TOML fetch
appName header interceptor is added to a shared module-level client, so one Server's X-App-Name is sent on every Server's requests
Paging next()/prev() follow Horizon-supplied absolute links to arbitrary hosts
Absolute _links hrefs from Horizon responses are fetched without a host check
stellar.toml fetch follows HTTP redirects past the HTTPS-only default
Unbounded server Date header sets the transaction maxTime window

failing_checks.title: Replay and double payment
failing_checks.reason: The SDK does not retry (server.ts:309, one POST). But after the POST succeeds, decoding of result_xdr at server.ts:322-326 can throw (for example on a protocol 23 result shape). The caller gets a rejection with no hash. A caller that retries by rebuilding the transaction with a fresh sequence number

failing_checks.title: Submission outcome
failing_checks.reason: submitTransaction sends with a 60 s timeout (server.ts:314). It does not return the envelope hash on failure. It also decodes result_xdr after the send (server.ts:317-326), and any decode error becomes a rejection even though the transaction may have applied. Success is not checked against the respo

failing_checks.title: Failure and rollback paths
failing_checks.reason: The pre-send paths (memo lookup server.ts:298-300, challenge checks utils.ts:118-272) throw before any state change, so they are fine. The failure path after a successful send is not: the post-send decode at server.ts:322-326 rejects with no hash, so the caller cannot reconcile the payment as landed

failing_checks.title: Tenant isolation
failing_checks.reason: Multiple Server instances (one per tenant) share the module-level HorizonAxiosClient. Each appName constructor adds an interceptor that is never removed, so the X-App-Name header is not keyed by the Server that issued the request.
